analysis:
This is a documentation-only change to docs/reference/configuration.md. The head diff changes the date at line 3, line 371 and lines 568 and 584-590. Lines 568 and 584-590 fall outside the supplied units. Their base ranges (567, 583-584) were not visible either, so that later part of the change is a coverage limit.

The one security-relevant addition is head line 371, DARKBLOOM_VERIFIED_WEIGHTS_FILE (default ~/.darkbloom/verified-weights.json, read by VerifiedWeightHashStore.swift). It is an owner-only persisted record of fully verified managed-load weight hashes. Each record is bound to every file's device, inode, size, mtime and ctime. Startup registration reuses a matching record instead of re-hashing.

This touches A-004, T-012, T-027 and TB-003. The record and its env-path override are operator-controlled, ADV-001. An operator with root or a filesystem able to preserve inode and time metadata could replace weights while keeping the metadata. An operator could also edit the JSON directly, so registration reports a stale or forged hash. Per A-004/T-012, however, the weight hash is already provider-self-reported and not cryptographically protected against the operator. The supplied evidence therefore does not establish a regression.

It is also unverified whether this cache feeds only registration, or also the managed-load byte verification that line 31 says checks manifest-pinned bytes. Questions for integration and source review:
- Does the store skip actual load-time verification?
- Is DARKBLOOM_VERIFIED_WEIGHTS_FILE forwarded to launchd?
- Is the file opened no-follow with owner-only permissions?
- Should the T-012/A-004 notes document this cache as an operator-tamperable trust record?

The remaining text was examined against T-041 and is unchanged in the visible ranges:
- Prefix-cache defaults at lines 54-57 and 439, and the MiMo complete-prefix control at line 461.
- GLM local qualification, endpoint resumption/logout (lines 137-158, A-008, T-053) and App Attest worker flags (lines 211-227, TB-011).

No concrete regression was identified.
